findings.english_quote: as did the one who made it
findings.issue: The masculine αὐτόν refers naturally to the man under discussion, not to the neuter ζῷον represented by English “it.” The draft changes whose maker is being mentioned. Its note discusses the elliptical comparison but incorrectly assumes that the pronoun refers to the creature.
findings.suggested_revision: Replace this phrase with “as did the one who made him.” Revise the note to distinguish the comparatively clear masculine referent from the ambiguity concerning the predicate understood in the comparison.

findings.source_quote: ὁ δὲ ἕτερος, ὡς „υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου“ ἄρσην ὢν, καὶ τὰ διαφέροντα ὡς ἄρσενι τῷ μέλλοντι αἰῶνι προφητεύει.
findings.english_quote: But the other, being male as “Son of Man,” also prophesies the superior things, as befits a male, for the age to come.
findings.issue: The dative ἄρσενι belongs with τῷ μέλλοντι αἰῶνι: the coming age is characterized as male. The draft instead makes the phrase sound like a statement about what befits the male prophet, adding a notion of propriety and obscuring the age’s gender. No note discloses this attachment decision.
findings.suggested_revision: Attach the male characterization explicitly to the age, for example: “But the other, being male as ‘Son of Man,’ also prophesies the superior things for the coming age as a male age.” Explain the agreement of ἄρσενι with αἰῶνι and the contrast with the present world. Any revised sentence requires fresh review.

findings.english_quote: but also believes that she herself will become one
findings.issue: πιστοῦσα has an assuring or confirming force; it is not simply the ordinary πιστεύουσα, “believing.” The draft substitutes a statement of her belief for the assurance or claim she makes, without a note supporting that lexical choice or preserving the alternative.
findings.suggested_revision: Use a rendering such as “but also gives assurance that she herself will become one.” If retaining “believes” or “is confident,” provide a defensible lexical and contextual account of that use of πιστοῦσα and disclose the assurance/confirmation alternative.

findings.source_quote: ἐλπίδι τοῦ γενέσθαι ὃ μὴ ἔχει φύσιν καὶ ὃ ἔχει προσαπολλύουσα
findings.english_quote: in the hope of becoming what she does not have by nature, she also destroys what she does have
findings.issue: The note discloses an impersonal relative-clause alternative, but omits the material reading in which ἔχει φύσιν concerns possessing the nature or natural capacity to become something. Its description of φύσιν as adverbial does not explain the proposed accusative-of-respect analysis. The existing contextual rendering should not be treated as uniquely established.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare the main text explicitly with “in the hope of becoming what she lacks the nature to become, she also destroys what she does possess.” Preserve the natural-capacity reading alongside the disclosed impersonal alternative. If retaining the present wording, explain its grammatical analysis and why that contextual reading was chosen.

findings.source_quote: ὡς ζηλοῦν αὐτοῦ μέλλοντος ἐν τοῖς ἐσομένοις ἢ γυναῖκα ἢ κτήματα ἢ τὴν τῶν γονέων πρὸς αὐτὸν στοργήν.
findings.english_quote: since in what was to come he was destined to be jealous of him over either a wife or possessions or the parents’ affection for him.
findings.issue: αὐτοῦ is the genitive subject of μέλλοντος, whose complementary infinitive is ζηλοῦν. It does not supply an additional person whom Cain envies. The draft uses it both for “he” and for the added “of him,” introducing an unsupported target of jealousy. The note consequently preserves a pronoun ambiguity that this part of the Greek does not contain; the later αὐτόν is a separate referent question.
findings.suggested_revision: Remove “of him”: “since in what was to come he was destined to be jealous over either a wife or possessions or the parents’ affection toward him.” Correct the note to explain αὐτοῦ as the subject of μέλλοντος and discuss any uncertainty concerning the later πρὸς αὐτόν separately.

findings.issue: The second source quotation includes καὶ, whereas the draft places “and” outside that quotation. The substantive assertion survives, but the quotation boundary is not preserved.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain “and” within the second quotation, for example: “For he was a ‘murderer’ ‘and liar,’ …”, using the draft’s normal quotation-mark style and adjusting surrounding punctuation for readability.

findings.source_quote: διὸ καὶ ἡ τῶν ἐγγόνων προφητεία, μοιχῶν καὶ ψαλτηρίων γέμουσα, λανθανόντως διὰ τῶν ἡδυπαθειῶν ὡς τοὺς πολέμους ἐγείρει.
findings.english_quote: Therefore the prophecy of the descendants too, full of adulterers and harps, secretly stirs up wars through sensual pleasures, as it were.
findings.issue: “As it were” introduces a hedge suggesting that the stirring up of wars is figurative or qualified. Here ὡς precedes the finite clause τοὺς πολέμους ἐγείρει. The note lists the viable exclamatory reading “how …!” but gives no grammatical or contextual basis for the chosen standalone hedge. Listing alternatives does not itself support that main rendering.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider the defensible exclamatory construction: “Therefore the prophecy of the descendants too, full of adulterers and harps—how it secretly stirs up wars through sensual pleasures!” Preserve the interpretive uncertainty in a note. If another modal reading is retained, substantiate its construction rather than merely assigning ὡς a qualifying function. No print-verification block is established by this ambiguity.
